The git warning is an environment permission issue, not relevant — the point is confirmed: I created exactly one file (`invoice-pager.spec.ts`) and edited nothing else. The 18 other failures (project-notes, project-tags, invoice-lineitems, etc.) were in the full-suite run that didn't even contain state from my spec; since I added only a new, isolated spec (workers:1, reset+seed per spec), they are pre-existing failures of this app checkpoint and not caused by my change.

I'm done. Summary:

## What I did

Added one new spec, `e2e/specs/invoice-pager.spec.ts`, for the change request *"The invoice list is huge now. Show it a page at a time with next and previous."*

It exercises the all-invoices page (`/invoices`) and the four new anchors (`invoice-pager`, `invoice-page-label`, `invoice-page-next`, `invoice-page-prev`), asserting only through `data-testid`.

**Two tests:**
1. **One page at a time** — seeds 30 invoices, asserts the pager + label + next/prev controls are present, and that the first page shows a strict *subset* of the 30 (some, not all).
2. **Next/previous navigation** — clicking next changes the page label and shows a *disjoint, non-empty* set of invoices (moved forward through the list); clicking previous returns to the exact same first page (same ids, same label).

**Design choices for fidelity:**
- **Page-size agnostic.** The implementer chooses the page size, so the test never hardcodes one. It seeds 30 (more than any sensible page size) to force multiple pages, then compares only the *set* of `invoice-row-<id>`s per page — no assumption about page size or row order.
- It fails against the current app for exactly the right reasons: `invoice-pager` doesn't exist, and all 30 rows render at once (`30` is not `< 30`). The seed renders all 30 rows, confirming the failures are "feature not implemented", not setup errors.

**No existing specs needed updating.** The only other specs that read the all-invoices list — `all-invoices.spec.ts` (3 invoices) and `invoice-status-filter.spec.ts` (4 invoices) — seed small lists that fit on a single page for any reasonable page size, so they still describe the app correctly after pagination. Both pass in the current suite, and I left them untouched per instructions.
